pins.title: A warm hat with a light built in
pins.sub: For dark evening walks and chores.
pins.pinTitle: LED beanie with a rechargeable light: warm knit hat with hands-free light for dark winter walks
pins.description: After the clocks go back, the walk to the car and the evening dog walk happen in the dark. This cuffed knit beanie has a 4-LED light in the front cuff, three brightness levels and a light unit that plugs straight into USB to charge. One adult size, seven colors. For real night hikes, carry a proper headlamp too.

pins.title: Rocky trail? Give your dog a handle.

Reflective edging for dusk walks, two quick-release buckles, sizes S to XL for dogs about 9 to 110 lb (4 to 50 kg). Gear ships in 6-13 business days.

pins.title: Chilly morning hike? Bring a fleece.

pins.title: Cold floor under your desk?

pins.title: Plan your hike before you lace up

pins.description: A good day hike starts at home: pick a trail that fits your group, check the weather and sunset time, plan water and a turnaround time, and leave your route with someone. Our step-by-step guide to planning a hike, for beginners.

pins.title: A short family hike before the feast
pins.sub: Easy trails with a toddler in tow.

pins.description: A slow holiday-morning walk with a little one: pick a short, easy trail, dress them warmer than you (a toddler in a carrier moves less), pack snacks and plan to turn around early. In late fall many states have hunting seasons, so wear blaze orange and check your state wildlife agency for dates. Our 24-page printable guide for hiking with babies and toddlers.

pins.title: Hiking alone? Make a plan first.

pins.description: Hiking alone can be calm and freeing with the right habits: leave a trip plan with someone, know your turnaround time and carry the essentials. Our printable solo hiking guide covers it step by step. In hunting season, wear blaze orange. Instant PDF download.
